title: .NET Compact Framework
summary: The .NET Compact Framework is a scaled-down version of the .NET Framework designed for resource-constrained mobile and embedded devices such as PDAs, mobile phones, and factory controllers. It uses a subset of the full .NET class libraries plus mobile-specific controls, running on a JIT compiler optimized for limited hardware. Development occurs primarily in Visual Studio using C# or Visual Basic .NET, producing applications that require the runtime to execute. The UI layer is built on Windows Forms, which inherits a desktop-oriented design, making modern touch-screen interfaces difficult without third-party controls. The 3.5 release added features like LINQ and WCF, while later versions introduced multi-core support. The Xbox 360 variant further restricts the class library and limits thread counts, though it allows processor affinity settings.

mechanisms.title: Scaled class libraries
mechanisms.explanation: The framework uses a reduced set of the full .NET class libraries along with mobile-specific controls, scaled down to conserve space on constrained devices.

mechanisms.title: JIT compilation for mobile devices
mechanisms.explanation: Applications run on a specialized, high-performance just-in-time compiler designed for mobile-device execution rather than the full desktop runtime.
